thesis: Held position. Microsoft reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-07-29: CNBC reports revenue of $90.01B against $87.62B expected and adjusted EPS of $4.74 against $4.24 expected, with Azure growth accelerating to 43% year over year and the cloud platform passing $100B in annual revenue for the first time; M365 Copilot was disclosed at over 30 million paid seats. The stock rose 15.5% on 2026-07-30, its largest single-day move since 2020. The strongest counter-case is that part of the headline beat is non-operating rather than earned: Microsoft cited a $3.2B gain on its Anthropic investment and lower-than-expected costs from its first voluntary retirement program, so the EPS line flatters the quarter. That does not change the read, because the Azure acceleration to 43% and the $100B annualized cloud milestone are operating disclosures that stand independently of both one-offs, and it is those, not the EPS line, the thesis rests on. Also noted and not flagged: a £2.1bn UK Competition Appeal Tribunal claim over cloud licensing went to trial in June 2026 with a full trial scheduled during 2026, and a securities class action is open whose lead-plaintiff deadline (2026-08-11) has already passed; this run's research did not establish a specific scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance date falling inside the next ~90 days, so neither is treated as a risk flag.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates back toward the high-30s in the next quarterly disclosure, or a subsequent filing shows the cloud revenue milestone was reached on one-time or related-party contributions rather than recurring consumption

thesis: Held position. The most recent confirmed disclosure is fiscal Q1 2027 (reported May 2026): record revenue of $43.8B, up 88% year over year, with $16.1B of AI server revenue (reported up 757% year over year), non-GAAP EPS of $4.86, and a $51.3B backlog; management raised full-year revenue guidance toward $167B and roughly $60B of AI server revenue. On 2026-08-04 AI cloud startup Volta announced a $10B partnership naming Dell as technology provider for a 133MW facility in Norway. The 60-day tape agrees with the disclosures — the stock is up 11.9% over the window and sits 8.6% below its 52-week high — so there is no adverse move to reconcile. This does not reach high conviction for one specific reason: Dell reports fiscal Q2 2027 on 2026-08-28, two days from now, which is an unresolved binary catalyst falling before the next review and capable of reversing the read in either direction. This suggests the AI-server ramp is still intact, rather than confirming it through the coming print.
invalidation: the 2026-08-28 fiscal Q2 print shows AI server backlog converting more slowly than the $60B full-year figure implies, or the raised full-year guidance is walked back

thesis: Held position, and the case where the tape and the disclosures point opposite ways, so it was researched twice. The disclosure is unambiguously good: Astera Labs reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-04 with record revenue of $392.4M (reported up 104% year over year, though secondary outlets quote the growth rate inconsistently, so only the revenue figure is treated as firm) and guided fiscal Q3 to $540M-$560M, above analyst expectations and roughly 40% sequential growth at the midpoint. The tape did the opposite: the stock fell 12% the next day and is down 36.3% over the 60-day window, 40.5% below its 52-week high. The second search did not surface a company-specific negative to explain that: reporting attributes the decline to a broad AI/semiconductor selloff with no guidance cut, no lost customer and no product delay, a valuation reset from a forward P/E above 260x and roughly 40x expected 2026 revenue, and accelerating insider selling by executives and directors. The structural counter-case named in that research is customer concentration — one customer was reported as more than 70% of 2025 revenue, and the Scorpio X ramp depends on a handful of hyperscaler platforms. That counter-case is real and this run could not settle whether the de-rating is pricing it or merely unwinding a crowded position, so the evidence stays unresolved and the move reads as sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration. Holding is still supported by the disclosed beat and raised guidance, at the lowest conviction.
invalidation: the next quarterly disclosure shows the sequential step-up guided for fiscal Q3 was not delivered, or a filing discloses a change in the concentrated hyperscaler relationship

thesis: Held position, and the read is unresolved in the opposite direction from ALAB: the disclosed news is bad while the tape is strong. Research this run confirms a securities class action against Corcept and named executives covering purchases between 2024-10-31 and 2025-12-30, alleging the company projected confidence in the relacorilant NDA for hypercortisolism while the FDA had repeatedly warned in 2024 and 2025 pre-submission meetings that the clinical data lacked sufficient evidence of effectiveness; the suit follows an FDA rejection and a federal court patent loss, and one analyst reset its target to $67 from $105 against a current price of $119.78. The offsetting disclosure is that 2026 revenue guidance of $900M-$1.0B stands. The stock is up 36.3% over the 60-day window and sits 5.2% below its 52-week high, and this run's research did not identify any company-disclosed positive catalyst that accounts for that advance. So the counter-case here is the rally itself, it was engaged, and it could not be reconciled with the disclosed setbacks — the evidence is unresolved rather than net-positive. Holding is still supported by the standing revenue guidance, at the lowest conviction. The class action is described in this narrative but not flagged: this run's research established no specific scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline falling within the next ~90 days, and an open suit without a scheduled next step does not meet the active_litigation criterion.
invalidation: a scheduled court or FDA date inside the review horizon emerges, or 2026 revenue guidance is reduced from the $900M-$1.0B range

thesis: Largest signal this cycle: down 40.2% over the 60-day window and 42.5% below its 52-week high. The move is explained by disclosures this run read. Corning beat Wall Street estimates on both revenue and earnings for Q2 2026, but third-quarter guidance came in slightly below elevated consensus, which alone triggered a single-day decline of more than 20%. Optical Communications, the AI-driven growth segment, grew 32% year over year to $2.07B but decelerated from 36% in the prior quarter. Separately, reports that Apple scrapped its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone removed a specialty-glass program, and the shares fell 2.7% on that. A five-session stretch took roughly $24B off a market value now around $125B. The counter-case for buying the drawdown is that the quarter itself was a beat and the stock is still up 138.9% over the past year, so this may be an unwind of a crowded AI trade rather than a business problem. This run cannot settle that: the guide-down relative to consensus and the segment deceleration are company-specific and disclosed, while the rotation and profit-taking are not separable from them in the reporting read. With a decelerating growth engine and a cancelled customer program both on the record, this suggests waiting rather than entering.
invalidation: Optical Communications growth re-accelerates above the prior 36% rate in the next disclosure, or guidance is raised back above consensus

thesis: Down 33.0% over the 60-day window despite what this run's sources describe as a strong Q2 2026: Intel beat Wall Street on both the top and bottom lines and topped third-quarter guidance estimates, yet the stock fell almost 8% the following session as investors digested 2026 capital expenditure guided above $20B, up from about $18B. The drawdown then deepened on financing rather than operations: Intel announced plans to sell shares to fund capex and working capital and the stock fell about 4% on 2026-08-24, with reporting citing figures of both $15B and $20B for the offering, so the size is not treated as confirmed here. Bank of America kept a Buy rating while cutting its target from $160 to $145, citing 4-5% EPS dilution from the offering. The counter-case is that Intel remains up 159.9% year to date in 2026, which leaves it exposed to profit-taking on any negative sector headline, and this run cannot separate how much of the 33% decline is the offering versus that unwind. The disclosed equity raise is what caps this: it is a real, near-term dilution of the very earnings the beat delivered. This suggests the operating turn is intact and being paid for with shareholder dilution, not that the drawdown is finished.
invalidation: the completed offering prices materially larger than the $15B-$20B range being reported, or the capex increase is not matched by the demand it was raised against in the next quarterly disclosure

thesis: Down 32.5% over the 60-day window and 55.6% below its 52-week high. Rocket Lab reported Q2 2026 after the close on 2026-08-11 with record revenue of $234M, up 62% year over year against a $231M consensus, a $2.36B backlog, and Q3 guidance of $250M-$265M versus a $238M estimate — so both revenue and guidance beat. Two disclosures cut the other way: adjusted EPS came in at -$0.08 against -$0.07 expected, and on Neutron the company said Stage 1 tank production still aligns with delivering the vehicle to the launchpad in Q4 2026 but stopped short of reaffirming a first flight before year-end. The counter-case for entering is precisely that revenue beat and record backlog. It does not settle the read, because the growth the shares are priced against — reporting puts the stock near 59 times revenue with Neutron still unflown — depends on a first flight the company itself declined to commit to. The evidence is therefore offsetting rather than net-positive, and the binary event that would resolve it has no committed date. This suggests waiting for a firm Neutron flight date rather than entering ahead of it.
invalidation: Rocket Lab commits publicly to a Neutron first-flight date, or the Q4 2026 launchpad delivery milestone slips explicitly into 2027

thesis: Down 31.0% over the 60-day window and 54.8% below its 52-week high, and unlike most names screened this cycle the disclosures explain it directly. AST SpaceMobile's Q2 2026 business update on 2026-08-10 reported revenue of $31.5M against a $35.18M consensus and an adjusted loss of $0.77 per share against $0.26 expected — a miss on both lines as reported. In July 2026 the company raised $1.15B gross through 1.625% convertible senior notes, a structure the reporting explicitly ties to investor concern about future dilution. Bank of America, UBS and Deutsche Bank all cut targets after the print. The counter-case is genuine: the company disclosed 13 satellites in orbit, a revenue backlog approaching $1.3B, and maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150M-$200M. It does not resolve the read, because a maintained full-year range sits awkwardly against a quarter that missed by roughly 10% on revenue and roughly tripled the expected loss, and this run found nothing reconciling the two. A confirmed miss plus a fresh convertible overhang suggests standing aside on a new position.
invalidation: the next quarterly disclosure puts revenue back on a path to the $150M-$200M full-year range, or the convertible overhang is retired without share issuance

thesis: Down 26.9% over the 60-day window. The quarter itself was a beat on both lines as reported — EPS of $39.25 against a $34.45 estimate and revenue of $8.97B against $8.39B — but the company guided fiscal Q1 revenue to $10.3B-$10.8B against an $11.16B estimate, a guide below consensus even though it implies large sequential growth. That is the disclosed reason the stock fell, and reporting describes three consecutive double-digit percentage declines and a roughly 20% month-to-date drawdown. The counter-case for buying it is that the guided range still represents substantial sequential revenue growth off a record quarter, and that part of the decline is described as institutional profit-taking and rotation out of chip names into hyperscalers after a 574% run. This run cannot settle which dominates: the guide-down is company-disclosed and the rotation is not separable from it in the available reporting, so the evidence is mixed rather than resolved. This suggests the memory upcycle is being re-rated rather than broken, but not that the entry point is established.
invalidation: fiscal Q1 revenue lands at or above the $11.16B consensus the guidance fell short of, or NAND pricing disclosures show the guided deceleration was conservative

thesis: Down 24.8% over the 60-day window, and this is a case where the company published metrics pointing opposite ways, so both are quoted. On the income statement fiscal Q4 2026 revenue was $2.05B, up 34% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.74, and management guided fiscal Q1 2027 to $2.2B-$2.4B revenue and $1.85-$2.05 non-GAAP EPS while citing strong demand and expanding capacity. On the cash statement the same fiscal year shows revenue up 22.5% while operating cash flow fell 87.5% to $79.5M, against $1.10B of capital expenditure for AI-optics capacity. The stock fell about 8% after the print, with reporting attributing it to those cash-conversion concerns rather than to the earnings lines, and fell a further 6-12% across sessions in a sector-wide optical and photonics selloff described as an expectation reset with no company-specific warning or guidance cut. That combination is the whole problem: a growing, well-guided P&L funded by capex that operating cash flow is no longer covering, plus a sector de-rating this run cannot separate from it. This suggests the demand is real and the funding of it is the open question, which is not a resolved basis for entry.
invalidation: operating cash flow recovers toward the level the reported revenue growth implies in the next disclosure, or the $1.10B capex program is scaled back without cutting the revenue guide

thesis: Down 24.2% over the 60-day window and 49.3% below its 52-week high, on a company whose operating disclosures this run reads as strong. Applied Optoelectronics reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-06 with EPS of $0.06 against a $0.01 estimate and revenue of $191.9M, up 86% year over year and a fifth consecutive record quarter, driven by AI datacenter optics and CATV; management guided Q3 revenue to $255M-$290M and adjusted EPS to $0.11-$0.26 as 800G and 1.6T products ramp, and said demand exceeds capacity through mid-2027. The decline is attributable to financing rather than to those numbers: the stock fell about 10% after hours when the company unveiled a further $600M at-the-market offering and extended the drop about 12.3% pre-market the following session. The counter-case for the bull side is that Wall Street largely kept Buy and Overweight ratings after earnings while trimming targets. This run cannot settle how much of a 49% drawdown from the high is dilution versus the same AI-optics de-rating that hit COHR and LITE, so the read stays unresolved. This suggests real demand being funded by repeated share issuance, which is why the dilution flag is set.
invalidation: the $600M ATM program is drawn substantially without the guided Q3 revenue step-up materialising, or the mid-2027 capacity-constrained demand statement is walked back

thesis: Down 18.1% over the 60-day window even though the window contains a very strong disclosure. Nebius reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-12 with revenue of $582.3M, up 454% year over year, and EPS of -$0.12 against a -$0.82 estimate; management raised its year-end contracted power target to 5GW, reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $3.0B-$3.4B, and the company announced a $27B five-year compute agreement with Meta Platforms. The stock rose roughly 34% on the day. The 60-day decline is therefore a function of where the window opens — near a late-June high — not of the quarter. The counter-case is on the funding side and is why conviction is capped: on 2026-08-24 Nebius closed a private offering of two tranches of convertible senior notes raising $5.75B to fund AI cloud expansion. That is a completed raise inside the last 90 days on a company whose guided full-year revenue is $3.0B-$3.4B, so the financing is larger than a year of revenue and the dilution path is not something this run could size. This suggests a contracted, disclosed demand pipeline being built out on borrowed and potentially convertible capital.
invalidation: the Meta agreement's contracted revenue does not begin appearing in quarterly disclosures on the schedule implied by the reaffirmed guidance, or further capital is raised before the 5GW target is reached

thesis: Down 18.1% over the 60-day window with no earnings event inside it — the drivers this run found are external and unresolved. First, policy: reporting says the administration decided to permit Apple to buy memory chips from Chinese suppliers including ChangXin, and Micron fell 5.5% in the first five minutes of trading on that. Second, litigation: Netlist has brought new ITC and federal court patent actions over DDR5 RDIMMs and MRDIMMs seeking exclusion orders that could block some Micron memory products from US import and sale. Third, repeated failures at the $1,000 level with the stock falling 7.1% to $897.77 on 2026-08-24 as memory names led a chip selloff. The counter-case is a company disclosure and a strong one: Micron has told investors it has completed price and volume agreements for its entire calendar 2026 high-bandwidth memory supply, HBM4 included. It does not settle the read, because a sold-out 2026 does not address either an import-exclusion order or a structurally larger Chinese competitor set, and both of those are binary outcomes this run cannot handicap. The Netlist actions are described here but not flagged: no specific scheduled ITC or court date inside the next ~90 days was established this run.
invalidation: the ITC declines to institute or denies the exclusion orders Netlist is seeking, or the reported policy change on Chinese memory suppliers is not confirmed by an official action

thesis: Down 15.7% over the 60-day window, and the Q2 2026 print on 2026-08-12 published metrics that point opposite ways, so both are quoted. Revenue missed: $180M against $194M expected. Adjusted profitability beat: a loss of 5 cents per share against 17 cents expected. On a GAAP basis the net loss was $450.5M, of which $386.6M was stock compensation. Alongside that, management raised 2026 revenue guidance to $880M-$890M, the CEO said AI demand is 'through the roof', and the company unveiled its CS-4 system; ARK Invest bought over $60M in August. The stock fell about 14% in extended trading on the print. The counter-case for the bull side — a raised full-year guide and an improved adjusted loss — is named and cannot be reconciled with a 7% revenue miss in the same quarter: a company that missed the current quarter while raising the full year is pushing revenue into the second half, and this run found nothing establishing what underwrites that. Stock compensation at 86% of the GAAP net loss also makes the adjusted figure the flattering one to quote, which is why the miss is quoted first. This suggests unresolved evidence, not an entry.
invalidation: Q3 2026 revenue lands on the trajectory the raised $880M-$890M full-year guidance requires, or a second consecutive revenue miss confirms the guide was not supportable

thesis: Down 15.0% over the 60-day window, and the dominant driver this run identified is mechanical rather than fundamental: around 319 million shares held by early employees and investors became eligible to trade, part of a staggered lockup that will release roughly 88% of SpaceX's 13 billion shares through 2027, and the stock fell back below its $135 IPO price on that supply. Two other disclosed items weigh: Chinese startup LandSpace landed the first stage of its Zhuque-3 rocket on a pad in northwest China, the first orbital-class booster recovery on land by a Chinese company, which is a direct competitive datapoint; and the reported financials show a net loss of $541M with a pretax margin around -38.3% while capital spending rose to $18.37B from $2.83B a year earlier. The counter-case is that a lockup-driven decline is supply, not information, and the shares recovered 21% from a Friday that Wall Street expected to crash. That is exactly why this reads low: the largest single explanation for the drawdown is a share-supply schedule that continues through 2027, so the price is being set by an unwind rather than by disclosure, and there is no company-specific catalyst to enter against.
invalidation: the remaining lockup tranches clear without further price pressure, or profitability turns positive against the reported -38.3% pretax margin

thesis: Down 11.8% over the 60-day window and 23.0% below its 52-week high, screened on the price-move criterion. The company-specific item this run confirmed is a large custom AI chip agreement with Google, reported at $120B, against a stock that has rallied 170% year to date on demand for custom AI silicon and networking. Analyst targets were raised into the print — Wells Fargo to $310 from $240, Susquehanna to $265 from $230 — and 38 analysts rate it Buy with zero Sells. The decisive fact for conviction is timing, not sentiment: Marvell reports fiscal Q2 2027 after the close on 2026-08-27, tomorrow, a confirmed date. That is an unresolved binary catalyst falling before the next review, so the rubric caps this at medium no matter how favourable the setup reads, and the setup being widely expected to beat cuts both ways — reporting notes the crowd is already positioned for one. The Google agreement is a disclosed contract rather than a rumour, which is what keeps this above the low tier; the pending print is what keeps it below the high tier.
invalidation: the 2026-08-27 fiscal Q2 print misses or guides below consensus, or the reported scale or timing of the Google custom-silicon agreement is revised in the disclosure

thesis: Down 10.9% over the 60-day window. AMD reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-04 with revenue of $11.54B, up 50% from $7.69B, beating on both the top and bottom lines, and the stock fell 5% the next session, with other reporting putting the drop as high as 8%. Two conflicting margin figures were published and both are quoted: one account reports a gross margin miss at 54% against a 56% consensus, driven by near-term costs from the Helios AI infrastructure ramp, while another reports adjusted gross margin at 56% alongside a 31% data center EBIT margin, with data center now 58% of revenue. The company also disclosed that gaming graphics revenue declined year over year as higher industry-wide component costs pushed card prices up. The counter-case for the drawdown being an opportunity is the 50% revenue growth itself. It does not resolve the read, because the explanation this run's sources give for the fall is an expectations reset rather than a disclosed deterioration — 'it was priced for an exceptional result, and this was not an exceptional result' — and a sentiment-driven move is not something a thesis can underwrite. This suggests the data-center franchise is compounding while the market re-prices what it will pay for it.
invalidation: the next disclosure shows gross margin still below the 56% consensus level once the Helios ramp costs anniversary, or data center revenue share stops expanding from 58%

thesis: The only qualifying candidate this cycle whose 60-day move is upward: up 10.3% over the window, and 11.1% below its 52-week high. Lumentum reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-08-11 with revenue of $1,006.3M, up 109.3% year over year and the first billion-dollar quarter in company history, landing inside its own $960M-$1.01B guidance. Full-year 2026 revenue was $3.01B. The company published two conflicting bottom lines for the year and both are quoted: non-GAAP net income of $782.3M against a GAAP loss of $6.9B tied to $7.8B of debt extinguishment, described in the filing coverage as a large non-cash item. Analysts raised targets after the print — JPMorgan to $1,280, Citi to $1,200, Mizuho to $1,140. The counter-case is that GAAP loss, and it was engaged rather than waved past: this run established what it is attributed to, but not whether the extinguishment was settled in cash or in shares, so its effect on the share count is unknown. That is unresolved evidence on a capital-structure event roughly twice the company's annual revenue, which is what holds this at low despite a record quarter inside its guided range.
invalidation: the next filing shows the $7.8B debt extinguishment was settled with material share issuance, or fiscal Q1 revenue falls back below the $1B quarterly level just reached
